= Crow cryptogram — "217 English letters" claim check (2026-10-14) =

== The claim as received ==

> "Look through research for 217 English letters from the crow cipher — it said it
> decrypted SECOM."

Answered as asked: the repository research record, the challenge's own publisher page
(live and archived), and public sources were searched for any statement that the
Crow's Cryptogram has been decrypted into **217 English letters** by **SECOM**.

== Verdict ==

**No such claim exists in the record.** The research says the opposite, and says it
in numbers:

- The Crow's Cryptogram is **unsolved in this repository**. The largest scan on
  record covers 6,480 unique 20-letter key-phrase candidates and 12,767
  decrypt-and-score events across both checkerboard-numbering modes, with
  **0 survivors** (`docs/crow-gemini-battery-2026-10-03-output.txt`).
- `docs/crow-source-check-2026-10-02.md`: "there is still no source-supported Crow
  plaintext or key phrase in the public material inspected… A solve claim should
  therefore remain provisional unless it includes the key phrase, recovered
  plaintext, and an exact 600-digit re-encryption match."
- The publisher's page (fetched 2026-10-14; the 2022-02-16 Wayback capture agrees)
  publishes only the 600-digit ciphertext, the six-line hint, the statement "The text
  is in English, encrypted with nothing more than pencil, paper and a secret key
  phrase", and the table of honor (Oleksii Sylichenko 08 Feb 2023; Daisuke Kondo
  05 Sep 2026). **It publishes no plaintext, no key, and no letter count.**
- In the Crow material the string `217` occurs only inside the ciphertext itself
  (`… 22682 21731`, line 4 of 12). It is not a letter count of anything.

== What the record *does* say was decrypted ==

There is exactly one decryption in this line of research, and it is of **SECOM's own
worked example**, not of the Crow:

- SECOM page example: plaintext `RV TOMORROW AT 1400PM TO COMPLETE TRANSACTION USE
  DEADDROP AS USUAL`, key `MAKE NEW FRIENDS BUT KEEP THE OLD`, 105-digit ciphertext.
- `python3 tools/secom_probe.py` → `official SECOM 105-digit encrypt/decrypt vector:
  PASS`. The CyberChef `secomExact` op reproduces it too
  (`test/cyberchef-field-museum.test.ts`).
- The same exact model run **on the Crow** with the best-known opening-line candidate
  returns letter soup — `OYSASOXVEMSA 0OYVEAAPSFPSMSFITOTSHAOSHSS…` — a recorded
  rejection, not a solve.

So "it decrypted SECOM" is true of the *system's published example*. It has never
been true of the Crow ciphertext.

The other decrypt-shaped results in the suite are unrelated: the Enigma plugboard
benchmark (`EN RT OS AI`, synthetic Enigma data — see
`docs/crow-cryptogram-stecker-audit-2026-10-02.md`), and the ArcaneChat lab's own
training cryptogram (`MEET AT THE OLD OAK`, regenerated on every **NEW CROW** press).

== Why a 217-letter claim fails SECOM's own arithmetic ==

SECOM's straddling checkerboard encodes each plaintext symbol in **one digit** (exactly
seven letters) or **two digits** (every other letter, the space, the numerals), and
the publisher caps padding at **≤ 4 null digits** ("up to four null digits could be
added to complete a block of five" — SECOM page). That fixes an identity any claimed
plaintext length must satisfy:

```text
600 - pad = a + 2 * (T - a),   pad ∈ [0, 4],   0 <= a <= L <= T
```

where `T` is the number of plaintext symbols (letters + spaces + numerals), `L` the
letters among them and `a` the symbols written in a single digit. The identity is
self-checked in the tool against the publisher's worked example: 67 symbols (53
letters, 10 spaces, 4 numerals), 30 one-digit symbols → 104 digits, completed to 105
with one null digit. PASS.

Consequences for the Crow's 600 digits:

| Claimed plaintext | Symbols at 4.7 letters/word | Digits it can write | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 217 letters (the claim) | 263 | 309–526 | **REJECTED** — 70+ digits short of 596 even at maximum padding |
| 300 letters | 364 | 428–728 | arithmetically possible (one-digit share 43%) |
| 324 letters | 393 | 462–786 | possible only if the key's seven letters are the seven commonest |

- **T ≥ 298 symbols.** 217 letters would allow at most 81 non-letter symbols
  (space/numerals) — i.e. ≤ 2.68 letters per word, against 4.7 in ordinary English
  prose. Closing the digit shortfall would need 35+ two-digit null pairs against a
  documented allowance of 4 digits.
- **The English-prose window for 600 SECOM digits is 252–324 letters**: 252 if the
  key's seven one-digit letters are the seven rarest in English (Z Q J X K V B,
  ~3.7% share), 324 if they are the seven commonest (E T A O I N S, ~57.5%). A genuine
  English plaintext of the Crow should therefore sit in the low 300s of letters.
- The claim is not *strictly* impossible — a telegraphic 217-letter text with ≥ 81
  spaces would fit — but it matches no source, no published hint, and no analysis in
  this repository.

The falsifier is executable:

```sh
python3 tools/crow_letter_count_bounds.py 217 300 324
```

== Search log (what "look through research" covered) ==

- **Repository, all file types**: `217 letters`, `217 English`, `two hundred
  seventeen`, and a standalone-`217` scan of every file that mentions "crow". Hits:
  the ciphertext group `21731`, the patch holding it, and unrelated offsets/hashes in
  other projects (Dr. Solomon disassembly, WiMAX, Z-Library SHA-256, `slip44.json`).
  Nothing in any `docs/crow-*.md`, `tools/secom_*.py`, `tools/crow_gemini_battery.py`,
  `tools/search_crow_extractions.py`, `apps/Cipher-Machines-and-Cryptology-Suite-*.html`,
  the `sync-outgoing/` bundle and patch, or the `.arena-drive`/`.arena-archive`
  request manifests.
- **Git history**: `git log --all -S "217 letters"`, `-S "217 English"`,
  `--grep 217` — no commit in the repository's history has ever contained the claim.
- **Publisher**: live `crow.htm` plus the 2022-02-16 Wayback capture — no plaintext,
  no length, no key, and the older capture still says "unsolved to this day".
- **Web**: the Crow's Cryptogram, the Crow Language cipher from the *Catastrophe Crow*
  ARG (a monoalphabetic substitution, no SECOM content) and
  `adam.levav.net/CrowCiphers` (a Crow/Vigenère teaching page) are different puzzles;
  no page ties 217 letters to this ciphertext or to a SECOM decryption.

== What a real Crow solve has to include ==

Unchanged from `docs/crow-source-check-2026-10-02.md`: the 20-letter key phrase, the
recovered plaintext, an exact re-encryption of all 600 digits with ≤ 4 null digits,
and the transposition-invariant histogram match. A length alone is not evidence; a
length that contradicts SECOM's own arithmetic is a refutation.

If the "217 English letters" figure came from a chat, a generated summary or a page,
it can be turned into a verdict in one line:

```sh
python3 tools/crow_letter_count_bounds.py 217
```

== Reproduce ==

```sh
python3 tools/crow_letter_count_bounds.py 217 300 324   # claim check + model self-check
python3 tools/secom_probe.py                            # official vector PASS, Crow candidates rejected
node --test tests/crow-letter-count-bounds.test.mjs     # regression test for this note
```
